answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring every new identity to lock a jade-denominated bond for a fixed period before it can earn trust or vote. Existing agents randomly audit its signed transactions; a proven double-spend, copied policy, or coordinated fraud burns the bond and lowers the identity’s trust score below a preset delta threshold. Creating a Sybil swarm therefore costs the attacker one capital deposit per identity, ties that capital up, and makes hollow accounts unprofitable once expected slashing exceeds gains.
